finalText:
It's a small Node HTTP API, five files, no framework and no real database yet.

1. **`server.js`** — the entry point. Checks the bearer token on every request, then hands it to the route table.
2. **`auth.js`** — signs and checks tokens as `<userId>.<hmac signature>`, using a shared secret from `AUTH_SECRET`.
3. **`routes.js`** — a table mapping `METHOD /path` to handlers. Reads go through the cache, writes go straight to the store.
4. **`store.js`** — an in-memory map standing in for a real database. Every record expires 15 minutes after its last write.
5. **`cache.js`** — a 256-entry LRU cache in front of the store, just to absorb repeated reads.

One thing worth knowing before you build on this: `routes.js` says writes should invalidate the cache, but `putOrder` never does that. So after someone posts an order, `GET /orders` can keep serving the stale cached list until it ages out of the LRU on its own.
